title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: in the 'deuxième mouture' of Analysis situs (June 1986), Grothendieck axiomatizes 'tame' stratified spaces in two ways. One is abstract: posets of figures (F, ≤, ≪) satisfying axioms At1–At7. The other is concrete: a set M with a family F_M ⊂ Fig(M) of M-figures (finite stratifications by strates and multistrates) satisfying axioms At*/Ax*. Page 31 ends with the corollary that if Φ ⊂ Ψ in F_M then Φ is closed in Ψ, hence a sub-figure.

Bracketed remark (top half). On M ≃ M* (points identified with strates/multistrates) one gets a partial order: X ≤ Y iff P_{Omb(X)} ⊂ P_{Omb(Y)}, equivalently Omb(X) ∈ P_{Omb(Y)}. Here Omb is the 'ombre' (shadow) of X, and P_{Omb(Y)} is the set of shadows below Omb(Y), which Grothendieck names by definition 'Microomb(Y)' (or 'Multomb(Y)'). This order is chosen so that the elements F of F̃ are closed subsets, i.e. down-sets, of M for the Alexandrov topology of ≤.

Sending X to X̃ = M_{≤X} = {Y : Y ≤ X} gives an injection M ↪ F̃ (≃ F_M). It identifies M with the irreducible elements of F̃, ordered by inclusion. This is the Birkhoff/Alexandrov reconstruction of a poset from its lattice of (finitely generated) down-sets via its join-irreducibles.

Then comes a 'Théorème-Scholie'. The category of (groupoidal) stratifications (F, ≤, ≪) satisfying At1–At7 is equivalent to the category of pairs (M, F_M) with F_M ⊂ Fig(M) satisfying At*1, … . At*1 says F_M contains ∅ (hence is non-empty) and is stable under finite unions, the unions being joins in F_M. A further remark, partly illegible, says stability under ∧ is equivalent, given the next axiom, to stability under passing to closed 'figured' zones.

So the page states a representation/duality theorem: abstract posets of figures are realized as concrete families of figures on a point-set. It serves the programme of a purely combinatorial-order-theoretic foundation for tame topology. The remaining axioms (Ax*2–Ax*5: canonical multistrate on each strate, gluing, point separation) are on the next page.
errors: The image of X ↦ M_{≤X} in a lattice of down-sets ordered by inclusion consists of the join-(∨-, sup-)irreducible elements, not the meet-irreducible ones. Either the transcription's '∧' is a misreading (the image looks like 'sup.'/'str.') or Grothendieck slipped.
The equivalence 'P_{Omb(X)} ⊂ P_{Omb(Y)} iff Omb(X) ∈ P_{Omb(Y)}' tacitly requires P_A to be a down-closed family containing A. This is plausible from context but is not stated on the page.

The Théorème-Scholie is only stated, not proved. The list of axioms At*1… is unfinished on this page, and the next page ends 'J'espère que je n'ai pas oublié d'axiomes!', so completeness of the axiom set is unverified.

ideas.what: Order on points/strates defined via inclusion of shadow families, making figures closed (down-closed) subsets
ideas.modern_name: Specialization order / Alexandrov topology of a finite poset-stratified space
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937); in stratified homotopy theory, poset-stratified spaces (MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie HA Appendix A)

ideas.what: Reconstruction of M as the irreducible elements of the lattice of figures via principal down-sets M_{≤X}
ideas.modern_name: Birkhoff representation theorem (join-irreducibles of a distributive lattice of down-sets)

ideas.what: Théorème-Scholie: equivalence between abstract (groupoidal) stratifications (F, ≤, ≪) satisfying At1–At7 and concrete pairs (M, F_M ⊂ Fig(M)) satisfying axioms At*
ideas.modern_name: Stone/Birkhoff-type duality between abstract posets of stratifications and point-set stratified structures; cf. o-minimal/tame topology foundations
ideas.usually_credited_to: No direct counterpart; Esquisse d'un programme (1984) calls for 'topologie modérée' but contains no such axiomatics
ideas.where_published: Programmatic only in Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 (tame topology); this axiomatization appears unpublished

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates an order-theoretic duality: abstract posets of figures with relations ≤ (sub-figure) and ≪ correspond to concrete point-set families of stratifications. Tame stratified spaces would then be reconstructed from purely combinatorial lattice data, with points recovered as irreducibles. The axiom list is left incomplete and the proof is not given.
missed.quote: Théorème-Scholie La catégorie des (groupoïdales) stratifications (F,≤,≪) satisfaisant à : At 1 à At 7, équivalente à celle des (M,F_M)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Current stratified homotopy theory (exit paths, poset-stratified spaces, Ayala–Francis–Tanaka, Haine) works with poset-stratified topological spaces and does not axiomatize the lattice of admissible stratifications itself. A worked-out version of this point-free 'lattice of figures' approach to tame topology does not appear to exist. It is, however, only sketched here.

deep.surprise_reason: The order-theoretic steps are standard (Alexandrov topology, Birkhoff representation). The unpublished element is the attempt at a categorical equivalence between abstract and concrete axiomatizations of stratified tame spaces, which is interesting but sketchy and unproved.
transcription_corrections: 'de telles [-façon-]' should read 'de telle façon' (with 'façon' struck).
'des éléments ∧-irréductibles' — the image looks more like 'sup.'/'str.' irréductibles; mathematically it should be join- (sup-) irreducible.
The 'Microomb(Y)' label above 'Omb(X) ∈ P_{Omb(Y)}' is uncertain; it may read 'Multomb(Y)'.
At*1 line: roughly 'F_M contient ∅ (non vide, et stable par réunions finies [‘un joins’ = ‘ou joins’] dans F_M)'.
Last lines: '[La stabilité par ∧ ... équivaut, moyennant la condition suivante, à celle de stabilité par passage à une zone figurée]' (partially illegible).
